lines.text: Many learners say: I want a coffee, please.
Better: I would like a coffee, please.
The second! I would like a coffee, please.

data.right: I would like a coffee, please.

native.tip: Em português, “eu quero um café” soa normal ao pedir; em inglês, “I want” soa seco. Use “I would like”.
native.caption: Você também pede assim? “I want a coffee, please.” 😅 Soa mais educado: “I would like a coffee, please.” Em português, “eu quero um café” soa normal ao pedir; em inglês, “I want” soa seco. Ouça a Ama e repita! Treine mais no app Lexkite.
native.comment: Resposta: “would like”. Agora escreva uma frase sua com “I would like” e treine mais com um quiz grátis aqui: {link}

en.tip: In Portuguese, “eu quero um café” sounds normal when ordering; in English, “I want” sounds blunt. Use “I would like”.
en.caption: Do you order like this? “I want a coffee, please.” 😅 It is more polite to say “I would like a coffee, please.” In Portuguese, “eu quero um café” sounds normal when ordering; in English, “I want” sounds blunt. Listen to Ama and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.
